75: ## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE
76: 
77: ### Problem Statement
78: The router sends four authoring intents to `references/templates/template-guide.md`, a 1,200-line guide. A weak model that loads it writes less, not more: it samples the guide and copies the nearest example. The guide also mixes template-authoring rules with packet-authoring rules, so a model that only needs to fill a scaffold reads rules about `.tmpl` files it must not touch.
79: 
80: ### Purpose
81: A weak model reaches one short card for the authoring intents, and the long guide is still one request away for a reader who needs it.
82: <!-- /ANCHOR:problem -->

87: ## 3. SCOPE
88: 
89: ### In Scope
90: - One card at `references/workflows/spec-authoring-card.md`, at most 260 lines, whose text is frozen in `plan.md` section 3.
91: - Four `RESOURCE_MAP` rows, for PLAN, IMPLEMENT, INTAKE and TEMPLATE_AUTHORING, that load the card.
92: - One `SKILL.md` prose sentence that records the guide as an `ON_DEMAND` resource.
93: - `leaf-manifest.json` and `leaf-aliases.json` regenerated with the shipped generator and its companion fix command.
94: - One checklist line that sends a reader to a rendered example or a scaffold instead of the templates root.
95: - One `Verify:` slot in the `Task Format` declaration of `templates/core/tasks.md.tmpl`.
96: - `check-card-sync.sh`, a vitest test that runs it, and a README row that lists it.
97: - Three Level 1 smoke runs of the card by a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash worker, measured with five commands.
98: 
99: ### Out of Scope
100: - Rewriting the template guide. Phase 2 owns the template and example defects, and phase 3 owns the guide's placeholder text. This phase only changes which tier loads the guide.
101: - Rewriting the filled example task lines. The card states the rule for new work, and phase 4 owns the example skeleton check.
102: - The full before-and-after benchmark. Phase 8 owns it, and this phase records a smoke test only.
103: - Any change to `references/templates/template-guide.md`.
104: 
105: ### Files to Change
106: 
107: | File Path | Change Type | Description |
108: |-----------|-------------|-------------|
109: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/workflows/spec-authoring-card.md` | Create | The card, copied from `plan.md` section 3 |
110: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/SKILL.md` | Modify | Four intent rows plus one prose sentence |
111: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/leaf-manifest.json` | Modify | Regenerated by `generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --write` |
112: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/leaf-aliases.json` | Modify | Regenerated by `ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs --fix --skill` |
113: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/workflows/spec-folder-authoring-checklist.md` | Modify | One pre-check line |
114: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/core/tasks.md.tmpl` | Modify | One `Task Format` line |
115: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/check-card-sync.sh` | Create | The sync guard |
116: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/README.md` | Modify | One row in the package topology list |
117: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/tests/card-sync.vitest.ts` | Create | Runs the guard in the suite |
118: | `specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/005-weak-model-authoring-card/scratch/card-bench/*` | Create | Three smoke runs and their metrics |
119: <!-- /ANCHOR:scope -->

125: 
126: ### P0 - Blockers (MUST complete)
127: 
128: | ID | Requirement |
129: |----|-------------|
130: | REQ-001 | `references/workflows/spec-authoring-card.md` exists, its line count is at most 260, and every command in it is one the phase ran or read from `--help` or source. |
131: | REQ-002 | In `SKILL.md`, the `RESOURCE_MAP` lists load the card for PLAN, IMPLEMENT, INTAKE and TEMPLATE_AUTHORING, and `references/templates/template-guide.md` appears in the `ON_DEMAND` list only. |

138: ### P1 - Required (complete OR user-approved deferral)
139: 
140: | ID | Requirement |
141: |----|-------------|

151: <!-- ANCHOR:success-criteria -->
152: ## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA
153: 
154: - **SC-001**: A worker told to follow the card reaches a `RESULT: PASSED` packet without opening the template guide.
155: - **SC-002**: A later edit that drops the card from one intent, or that moves the guide back into an intent, fails `check-card-sync.sh` and the suite.
156: <!-- /ANCHOR:success-criteria -->
157: 
158: ---
159: 
160: <!-- ANCHOR:risks -->
161: ## 6. RISKS & DEPENDENCIES
162: 
163: | Type | Item | Impact | Mitigation |
164: |------|------|--------|------------|
165: | Dependency | Phase 003 closed with the `v2.3` stamp and the token form | The card would teach a token form that does not exist | `tasks.md` T001 checks the stamp and the token on the real templates before the card is written |
166: | Dependency | Phase 004 closed with fill notes in each template section | The card would point at notes that are not there | The card names the note without quoting its shape, and T001 records what the notes look like |
167: | Risk | The card grows past 260 lines and becomes the guide again | A weak model samples it and the phase changes nothing | The guard fails above 260 lines and the card's own rule forbids a second topic per section |
168: | Risk | A worker copies from a `.tmpl` file and carries tokens into the packet | The packet fails strict or ships a token | The card's step 4 points at rendered examples, and the checklist line is changed in the same phase |
169: | Risk | The regenerated inventory rewrites another skill's files | A diff outside this phase's scope | The fix command runs with `--skill system-spec-kit` and T006 reads the file list it prints |
170: <!-- /ANCHOR:risks -->
171: 
172: ---
173: 
174: 
175: ## 7. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
176: 
177: ### Performance
178: - **NFR-P01**: The card stays at or below 260 lines, and each of its sections stays under 20 lines. A section over 20 lines is split or cut.
179: 
180: ### Security
181: - **NFR-S01**: The card and every brief carry no credential, token or key. Workers inherit provider login from the environment only.
182: 
183: ### Reliability
184: - **NFR-R01**: The guard is deterministic. Two runs on the same tree print the same lines in the same order, and it reads no network and writes no file.
185: 
186: ---
187: 
188: ## 8. EDGE CASES
189: 
190: ### Data Boundaries
191: - Empty input: a missing card makes the guard print `FAIL card-exists` and exit 1, never a stack trace.
192: - Maximum length: a card at exactly 260 lines passes, and 261 fails. The boundary is the `-le` test in the guard.
193: 
194: ### Error Scenarios
195: - External service failure: a provider error during a smoke run stops that run. The conductor records the error, retries once after 10 minutes, then records the run as failed.
196: - Network timeout: the smoke run is killed by its captured PID after 30 minutes and recorded as a failed run.
197: 
198: ---
199: 
200: ## 9. COMPLEXITY ASSESSMENT
201: 
202: | Dimension | Score | Triggers |
203: |-----------|-------|----------|
204: | Scope | 11/25 | Files: 9 changed, 1 created card, 3 measurement files. Systems: router, inventory, templates, checklist |
205: | Risk | 6/25 | Auth: N, API: N, Breaking: N, one shared router |
206: | Research | 12/20 | The card must match four scripts and two prior phases |
207: | Multi-Agent | 8/15 | Workstreams: card, router, guard, three smoke runs, one review |
208: | Coordination | 8/15 | Dependencies: phases 003 and 004 closed, launch preconditions |
209: | **Total** | **45/100** | **Level 3** |
210: 
211: ---
212: 
213: ## 10. RISK MATRIX
214: 
215: | Risk ID | Description | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
216: |---------|-------------|--------|------------|------------|
217: | R-001 | The card repeats the guide's scope and length | M | M | The 260-line guard, plus one topic per section |
218: | R-002 | A router edit lands in the wrong intent block | H | L | Each edit carries its intent header in the old text, so a wrong block cannot match |
219: | R-003 | The inventory fix writes outside system-spec-kit | H | L | `--skill system-spec-kit` scopes the run, and T006 reads the changed-file list |
220: | R-004 | A smoke run passes strict with tokens still in the packet | M | H | Metric M2 counts tokens separately from M1, and a run needs both to count as a pass |
221: 
222: ---
223: 
224: ## 11. USER STORIES
225: 
226: ### US-001: One short card is the default (Priority: P0)
227: 
228: **As a** weak authoring model, **I want** one short card that names the files, the steps and the checks, **so that** I finish a packet without sampling a long guide.
229: 
230: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ### US-002: Drift fails, not warns (Priority: P1)
235: 
236: **As the** operator, **I want** the card, the router, the inventory and the checklist checked by one command, **so that** a later edit cannot quietly undo this phase.
237: 
238: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
239: 
240: ---
241: 
242: <!-- ANCHOR:questions -->
243: ## 12. OPEN QUESTIONS
244: 
245: - None that block this phase. Every choice it needs is frozen in `goal.md` section 1.
246: - The card's exact text is frozen in `plan.md` section 3. A change to that text is an amendment to this phase, not an executor choice.
247: <!-- /ANCHOR:questions -->
248: 
249: ---
250: 
251: ## RELATED DOCUMENTS
252: 
253: - **Implementation Plan**: See `plan.md`
254: - **Task Breakdown**: See `tasks.md`
255: - **Verification Checklist**: See `tasks.md`
256: - **Decision Records**: See `plan.md` section L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
257:

55: ## 3. ARCHITECTURE
56: 
57: ### Pattern

61: - **The card**: one markdown file under `references/workflows/`. It is the only authoring doc the four intents load.

84: 
85: # Spec Authoring Card
86: 
87: This card is the short path. Follow the steps in order. Each step has one action, one acceptance line and one command. When the command prints what the acceptance line says, go to the next step.
88: 
89: `references/templates/template-guide.md` is the long guide. Read it only when this card sends you there.
90: 
91: ## 1. BOUNDS
92: 
93: You write one packet, in one folder. The folder is the one `create.sh` prints.
94: 
95: Allowed writes: the packet folder and its `scratch/` folder.
96: Forbidden: `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js`, `/speckit:save`. Do not edit `.skilled/`, another packet or a source file. Do not run `create.sh` twice.
97: 
98: Acceptance: you can name the packet folder and the one command you will run to check it.
99: Verify: `pwd` prints the repository root, and `ls <packet folder>` lists `spec.md`.
100: 
101: ## 2. PICK THE LEVEL
102: 
103: Run the level helper first.
104: 
105: ```bash
106: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh --loc <lines> --files <count>
107: ```
108: 
109: Use the level it prints. Do not raise the level yourself. The level decides which files the packet needs.
110: 
111: | Level | Files the packet needs |
112: |-------|------------------------|
113: | 1 | `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, and `implementation-summary.md` once implementation starts |
114: | 2 | the Level 1 files plus `acceptance-criteria.md` |
115: | 3 | the Level 2 files plus the architecture sections and the decision records |
116: 
117: Acceptance: the level in the scaffold header matches the level the helper printed.
118: Verify: `rg -n 'SPECKIT_LEVEL' <packet folder>/spec.md` prints one line with that level.
119: 
120: ## 3. SCAFFOLD
121: 
122: Create the packet with one command. Keep `--skip-branch` so no git state changes.
123: 
124: ```bash
125: bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/create.sh --skip-branch --level <level> --track <track> --short-name <two-to-four-words> "<one sentence>"
126: ```
127: 
128: The command prints the folder it made. Use that path for every later command.
129: 
130: Acceptance: the folder holds `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md` and `scratch/`.
131: Verify: `ls <packet folder>` lists those names.
132: 
133: ## 4. READ BEFORE YOU WRITE
134: 
135: Open one rendered example at the same level under `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/examples/level-<level>/`. Read `spec.md` and `tasks.md`.
136: 
137: Do not copy from a `.tmpl` file. A `.tmpl` file carries tokens and gate markers. The examples are filled and safe to imitate for shape.
138: 
139: Each section of your scaffold carries a fill note. The note says what that section needs. Read the note before you write the section. The note is the contract for that section.
140: 
141: Acceptance: you can say, in one sentence, what the first section of `spec.md` must contain.
142: Verify: `sed -n '1,40p' <packet folder>/spec.md` shows the fill notes.
143: 
144: ## 5. ONE ACTION PER SECTION
145: 
146: Each section does one job. Write one idea per paragraph. Do not repeat the same fact in two sections.
147: 
148: - `spec.md` states the problem, the scope, the requirements and the success criteria.
149: - `plan.md` states the approach, the files to change, the test plan and the dependencies.
150: - `tasks.md` states the ordered actions.
151: - `implementation-summary.md` states what changed and how it was checked. Write it last.
152: 
153: Do not put a task list in `spec.md`. Do not put requirements in `plan.md`.
154: 
155: Acceptance: every heading in the packet has content under it, and no heading holds content that belongs to another heading.
156: Verify: `rg -n '^## ' <packet folder>/spec.md <packet folder>/plan.md` lists the headings you filled.
157: 
158: ## 6. THE PLAN SHAPE
159: 
160: A plan has 3 or 4 steps. More than 4 steps means the feature is too large for one packet. Split it or raise the level.
161: 
162: Each step carries three lines:
163: 1. What the step does.
164: 2. The acceptance line: what is true when the step is done.
165: 3. The verify command: the command a reader runs, and the text it prints.
166: 
167: ```markdown
168: ### Step 1: Add the flag parser
169: 
170: Acceptance: `--quiet` is accepted and the default output is unchanged.
171: Verify: `bash script.sh --quiet` prints one line.
172: ```
173: 
174: Acceptance: `plan.md` holds 3 or 4 steps, and each step has an acceptance line and a verify command.
175: Verify: `rg -c '^### Step ' <packet folder>/plan.md` prints 3 or 4.
176: 
177: ## 7. TASK LINES
178: 
179: Every task line has one action, one file and one verify clause.
180: 
181: ```markdown
182: - [ ] T001 Add the quiet flag to the option parser (`runtime/cli/spec/script.sh`). Verify: `bash runtime/cli/spec/script.sh --quiet` prints one line.
183: ```
184: 
185: Rules:
186: - One action per task.
187: - Name the file in parentheses.
188: - End with `Verify:` and the command plus its expected output.
189: - Put the tasks in the order you will run them.
190: - Mark a task `[x]` only after its verify command printed the expected output.
191: 
192: Acceptance: every task line ends with a `Verify:` clause.
193: Verify: `rg -c 'Verify: ' <packet folder>/tasks.md` and `rg -c '^- \[ \] T[0-9]' <packet folder>/tasks.md` print the same number.
194: 
195: ## 8. FILL EVERY TOKEN
196:

625: ### Roles

637: ### Execution Rules
638: 
639: | Rule | Requirement |

641: | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. No two tasks write the same file, so no task is marked `[P]` |
642: | TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief |
643: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
644: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number. Each edit below names its old text |
645: | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |
646: | TASK-COPY | The card is copied from section 3.1, never retyped. A retyped card fails the vocabulary check or the line count |

675: /speckit:save, and any edit to a file not listed under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS.
676: ```
677: 
678: The role line is a focused persona summary in place of a full agent file, the small-context exception that `cli-opencode` rule 18 allows. It is declared here as that exception.
679: 
680: ### Dispatch Command
681: 
682: ```bash
683: cd "$WORKTREE" && SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode2 run --standalone \
684:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json \
685:   "$(cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/$TASK.txt")" </dev/null > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$TASK.jsonl" 2>&1 &
686: PID=$!; wait "$PID"; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$PID" 2>/dev/null
687: ```
688: 
689: `PHASE` is this folder's path and `WORKTREE` is the build worktree. Never kill by a name pattern. Kill only the captured PID.
690: 
691: ### Status Reporting Format
692: 
693: ```text
694: [T###] DONE | BLOCKED - one line of evidence
695: ```
696: 
697: Written as a row in the progress table of `goal.md` section 4.

699: ### Blocked Task Protocol
700: 1. Restore any file the task changed with `git restore --source=<start commit> -- <file>`.
701: 2. Mark the task `[B]` in `tasks.md` with the failing command and the first line of its output.
702: 3. Re-dispatch at most twice with the brief corrected for what failed. After the third failure on the same task, leave it `[B]` and continue with the next task.
703: 4. Stop the phase when two tasks are blocked, and write `STOP` with both task IDs in `goal.md` section 4.

708: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
709: 
710: ### ADR-001: One card replaces the guide as the default load
711: 
712: **Status**: Accepted
713: 
714: **Context**: Four authoring intents load a 1,200-line guide. A weak model samples a long doc and copies the nearest example. The guide also mixes template-authoring rules with packet-authoring rules, so a model that only needs to fill a scaffold reads rules about files it must not touch.
715: 
716: **Decision**: The four intents load a 170-line card. The guide stays in the `ON_DEMAND` list, so a reader who asks for the full guide still gets it.
717: 
718: **Consequences**:
719: - A weak model gets one screen of rules and a command per step.
720: - A reader who needs the guide's depth must ask for it. The card names the guide once, so the path is visible.
721: 
722: **Alternatives Rejected**:
723: - Shortening the guide in place: it would still be the default load, and phase 2 owns its defect repairs.
724: - Two cards, one for templates and one for packets: it doubles the surface the guard must read for a difference only a template author sees.
725: 
726: ### ADR-002: Generate the inventory, never hand-edit it
727: 
728: **Status**: Accepted
729: 
730: **Context**: `leaf-manifest.json` is byte-checked by `generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --check`, and `leaf-aliases.json` is checked as its projection by `ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs`. A hand edit passes one and fails the other.
731: 
732: **Decision**: Run `generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --write` then `ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs --fix --skill system-spec-kit`. The `--skill` scope keeps the write inside this skill.
733: 
734: **Consequences**:
735: - Both files agree with the tree and with each other.
736: - The fix command also reports other root metadata violations. A non-zero exit with the two files written is recorded, not treated as a write failure.
737: 
738: **Alternatives Rejected**:
739: - Adding the card row by hand: it survives until the next generator run and then disappears.
740: 
741: ### ADR-003: A shell guard plus one vitest test, not a validator rule
742: 
743: **Status**: Accepted
744: 
745: **Context**: The surfaces are skill files, not a spec folder. `validate.sh` reads a packet, so it cannot check a router. The post-edit router runs per edited file and returns no finding on failure, so it cannot hold a repo-wide invariant.
746: 
747: **Decision**: `runtime/cli/spec/check-card-sync.sh` holds the invariant and `runtime/cli/tests/card-sync.vitest.ts` runs it in the suite. The script is also listed in `runtime/cli/spec/README.md`.
748: 
749: **Consequences**:
750: - One command answers whether the four surfaces agree.
751: - The check costs one process per suite run and reads five files.
752: 
753: **Alternatives Rejected**:
754: - A validator rule: it would need a packet argument it does not have.
755: - A post-edit hook: a hook that cannot block is not a guard.

708: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
709: 
710: ### ADR-001: One card replaces the guide as the default load
711: 
712: **Status**: Accepted
713: 
714: **Context**: Four authoring intents load a 1,200-line guide. A weak model samples a long doc and copies the nearest example. The guide also mixes template-authoring rules with packet-authoring rules, so a model that only needs to fill a scaffold reads rules about files it must not touch.
715: 
716: **Decision**: The four intents load a 170-line card. The guide stays in the `ON_DEMAND` list, so a reader who asks for the full guide still gets it.
717: 
718: **Consequences**:
719: - A weak model gets one screen of rules and a command per step.
720: - A reader who needs the guide's depth must ask for it. The card names the guide once, so the path is visible.
721: 
722: **Alternatives Rejected**:
723: - Shortening the guide in place: it would still be the default load, and phase 2 owns its defect repairs.
724: - Two cards, one for templates and one for packets: it doubles the surface the guard must read for a difference only a template author sees.
725: 
726: ### ADR-002: Generate the inventory, never hand-edit it
727: 
728: **Status**: Accepted
729: 
730: **Context**: `leaf-manifest.json` is byte-checked by `generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --check`, and `leaf-aliases.json` is checked as its projection by `ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs`. A hand edit passes one and fails the other.
731: 
732: **Decision**: Run `generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --write` then `ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs --fix --skill system-spec-kit`. The `--skill` scope keeps the write inside this skill.
733: 
734: **Consequences**:
735: - Both files agree with the tree and with each other.
736: - The fix command also reports other root metadata violations. A non-zero exit with the two files written is recorded, not treated as a write failure.
737: 
738: **Alternatives Rejected**:
739: - Adding the card row by hand: it survives until the next generator run and then disappears.
740: 
741: ### ADR-003: A shell guard plus one vitest test, not a validator rule
742: 
743: **Status**: Accepted
744: 
745: **Context**: The surfaces are skill files, not a spec folder. `validate.sh` reads a packet, so it cannot check a router. The post-edit router runs per edited file and returns no finding on failure, so it cannot hold a repo-wide invariant.
746: 
747: **Decision**: `runtime/cli/spec/check-card-sync.sh` holds the invariant and `runtime/cli/tests/card-sync.vitest.ts` runs it in the suite. The script is also listed in `runtime/cli/spec/README.md`.
748: 
749: **Consequences**:
750: - One command answers whether the four surfaces agree.
751: - The check costs one process per suite run and reads five files.
752: 
753: **Alternatives Rejected**:
754: - A validator rule: it would need a packet argument it does not have.
755: - A post-edit hook: a hook that cannot block is not a guard.
756:

108: #!/usr/bin/env bash
109: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
110: # COMPONENT: CHECK CARD SYNC
111: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
112: # The authoring card is only useful when four surfaces agree: the card file,
113: # the router that loads it, the leaf inventory that lists it, and the checklist
114: # that sends a reader to a filled example. Each surface can be edited alone,
115: # and a reader then follows a path the others do not describe. This guard
116: # reads all four and fails on the first disagreement.
117: #
118: # Read-only. It writes no file and prints one PASS or FAIL line per check.
119: #
120: # Usage: check-card-sync.sh [--skill-root <path>]
121: # Exit codes: 0 every check passed, 1 one check failed, 2 bad invocation.
122: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
123: 
124: set -euo pipefail
125: 
126: SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
127: SKILL_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
128: 
129: while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
130:     case "$1" in
131:         --skill-root)
132:             [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || { echo "check-card-sync.sh: --skill-root needs a path" >&2; exit 2; }
133:             SKILL_ROOT="$2"
134:             shift 2
135:             ;;
136:         --help|-h)
137:             sed -n '2,14p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
138:             exit 0
139:             ;;
140:         *)
141:             echo "check-card-sync.sh: unknown option: $1" >&2
142:             exit 2
143:             ;;
144:     esac
145: done
146: 
147: CARD_REL="references/workflows/spec-authoring-card.md"
148: CARD="$SKILL_ROOT/$CARD_REL"
149: ROUTER="$SKILL_ROOT/SKILL.md"
150: LEAVES="$SKILL_ROOT/leaf-manifest.json"
151: ALIASES="$SKILL_ROOT/leaf-aliases.json"
152: CHECKLIST="$SKILL_ROOT/references/workflows/spec-folder-authoring-checklist.md"
153: MAX_LINES=260
154: STATUS=0
155: 
156: pass() { printf 'PASS %s\n' "$1"; }
157: fail_check() { printf 'FAIL %s: %s\n' "$1" "$2"; STATUS=1; }
158: 
159: # 1. The card exists and stays short enough to read in one pass.
160: if [ ! -f "$CARD" ]; then
161:     fail_check card-exists "missing $CARD_REL"
162: else
163:     LINES=$(wc -l < "$CARD" | tr -d ' ')
164:     if [ "$LINES" -le "$MAX_LINES" ]; then
165:         pass "card-exists ($LINES lines)"
166:     else
167:         fail_check card-length "$LINES lines, limit $MAX_LINES"
168:     fi
169: fi
170: 
171: # 2. Every authoring intent loads the card.
172: for INTENT in PLAN IMPLEMENT INTAKE TEMPLATE_AUTHORING; do
173:     if awk -v intent="$INTENT" '
174:         $0 == "    \"" intent "\": [" { inside = 1; next }
175:         inside && $0 == "    ]," { inside = 0 }
176:         inside && /spec-authoring-card\.md/ { found = 1 }
177:         END { exit(found ? 0 : 1) }
178:     ' "$ROUTER"; then
179:         pass "intent-$INTENT"
180:     else
181:         fail_check "intent-$INTENT" "does not load $CARD_REL"
182:     fi
183: done
184: 
185: # 3. The long guide is reachable only from the on-demand level.
186: GUIDE_IN_MAP=$(awk '
187:     /^RESOURCE_MAP = \{/ { map = 1; next }
188:     map && /^\}$/ { map = 0 }
189:     map && /"references\/templates\/template-guide\.md"/ { n++ }
190:     END { print n + 0 }
191: ' "$ROUTER")
192: GUIDE_ON_DEMAND=$(awk '
193:     /"ON_DEMAND": \[/ { od = 1; next }
194:     od && /^    \],$/ { od = 0 }
195:     od && /"references\/templates\/template-guide\.md"/ { n++ }
196:     END { print n + 0 }
197: ' "$ROUTER")
198: if [ "$GUIDE_IN_MAP" -eq 0 ] && [ "$GUIDE_ON_DEMAND" -eq 1 ]; then
199:     pass guide-on-demand-only
200: else
201:     fail_check guide-on-demand-only "in intent lists: $GUIDE_IN_MAP, in ON_DEMAND: $GUIDE_ON_DEMAND"
202: fi
203: 
204: # 4. The inventory lists the card and the identity projection agrees.
205: if jq -e --arg p "$CARD_REL" '.modes[].leaves | index($p) != null' "$LEAVES" > /dev/null; then
206:     pass leaf-manifest
207: else
208:     fail_check leaf-manifest "does not list $CARD_REL"
209: fi
210: if jq -e --arg p "$CARD_REL" '[.[] | select(.diskPath == $p)] | length > 0' "$ALIASES" > /dev/null; then
211:     pass leaf-aliases
212: else
213:     fail_check leaf-aliases "does not list $CARD_REL"
214: fi
215: 
216: # 5. The checklist sends a reader to a filled example, not the gated source root.
217: if rg -q 'Read templates from `\.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/`' "$CHECKLIST"; then
218:     fail_check checklist "still sends a reader to the templates root"
219: else
220:     pass checklist
221: fi
222: 
223: if [ "$STATUS" -ne 0 ]; then
224:     echo "CARD SYNC FAILED"
225:     exit 1
226: fi
227: echo "CARD SYNC OK"

**Error-recovery contract.** If a dispatch returns an auth error after pre-flight passed (OAuth expired or revoked), invalidate the cache, rerun `codex login`, and re-check before retrying. Never substitute a model the user didn't approve.

### Default Invocation (Skill Default)

**Default model + effort + tier**: `gpt-5.5` · `medium` reasoning · `fast` service tier. Balances speed, cost, and quality for the typical delegation.

> **Fan-out fallback:** a deep-loop lineage that pins no model runs **GPT Luna**. The family is named here on purpose, without a version or an effort tier, so this line does not go stale when the family ships a point release; the runner resolves the current id. A drift test keeps the two in the same family.

```bash
codex exec \
  --model gpt-5.5 \
  -c model_reasoning_effort="medium" \
  -c service_tier="fast" \
  -c approval_policy=never \
  --sandbox workspace-write \
  "<prompt>" </dev/null
```

The trailing `</dev/null` is not optional in a non-interactive dispatch; Rule 6 below explains what a backgrounded codex does to an inherited stdin.

**User override** (honor explicit user phrasing verbatim):

| User says | Resolve to |
|-----------|------------|
| (nothing specified) | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="medium" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| "Use gpt 5.5 high fast" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="high" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| "Use gpt 5.5 low" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="low" -c service_tier="fast"` (fast stays unless user drops it) |
| "Use gpt 5.5 xhigh" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="xhigh" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| "Use gpt 6 luna max" | `--model gpt-6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort="max" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| "Use gpt 5.6 terra high" | `--model gpt-5.6-terra -c model_reasoning_effort="high" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| "Use gpt 6 sol ultra" | `--model gpt-6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort="ultra" -c service_tier="fast"` |

Honor whichever dimensions the user names. Model stays on `gpt-5.5` and service tier stays on `fast` unless the user explicitly names a different model or tier; keep the reasoning effort within the chosen model's ceiling (see Model Selection below and the roster in [references/providers-and-models.md](references/providers-and-models.md)).

### Model Selection

`gpt-5.5` at `medium` on the `fast` service tier (`-c service_tier="fast"`) is the skill default for cross-AI delegation. Alternates: `gpt-6-luna` (≤ `max`), `gpt-5.6-terra` / `gpt-6-sol` (≤ `ultra`) — full roster, per-model effort ceilings, and the 8-level effort ladder in [references/providers-and-models.md](references/providers-and-models.md). Set effort with `-c model_reasoning_effort="<level>"` (there is **no `--reasoning-effort` flag**).

**Selection Strategy**: default `gpt-5.5 medium`; raise to `high` / `xhigh` for architecture, security, and complex planning; escalate the model when the task wants reasoning past `xhigh`; drop to `low` / `minimal` for trivial lookups. Per-task rationale table: [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) §5.

### Codex Agent Delegation

The calling AI is the conductor; Codex profiles in `$CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml` shape HOW Codex processes the task (sandbox, reasoning). Route with `-p <name>` when the task matches a specialization. Full roster and invocation patterns: [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md).

| Task Type | Profile |
|-----------|---------|
| Code review / security audit | `review` |
| Architecture exploration | `context` |
| Technical research | `research` (+ top-level `--search`) |
| Documentation generation | `write` |
| Fresh-perspective debugging | `debug` |
| Multi-strategy planning | `ai-council` |

Git diff review uses the built-in subcommand (no `-p`): `codex exec review "..." --commit HEAD`. Profiles may override `model`, `model_reasoning_effort`, `sandbox_mode`, `approval_policy`. The `.codex/agents/*.toml` files define personas for the interactive multi-agent TUI, NOT the `-p` flag.

### Dispatch-Critical Gotchas

The full flag glossary, sandbox modes, unique capabilities (`/review`, `--search`, `codex mcp`, session resume/fork, `--image`, `codex cloud`), essential command examples, and troubleshooting table are in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md). Five gotchas that break a dispatch, or make a child misreport its result, and must be honored at routing time:

- **`codex exec` defaults to `--sandbox read-only`** — file-modification tasks silently no-op (the agent plans changes but cannot write them). Pass `--sandbox workspace-write`; for headless no-prompt execution use top-level `-a never` before `exec` or `-c approval_policy=never`.
- **`--search` is a top-level flag, not an `exec` flag** — enable live web search as `codex --search exec …` (it precedes the subcommand). On codex ≥ 0.144 `codex exec --search` hard-fails with `unexpected argument '--search'` (older 0.125 builds accepted it), so treat any `exec … --search` example as stale. Without it, `codex exec` has no web access and answers from training data only — every dispatch needing live data (latest versions, repo facts, advisories) MUST use `codex --search exec …`.
- **Always pass `-c service_tier="fast"` explicitly** — this routes through the fast tier instead of whatever the caller's `~/.codex/config.toml` defaults to. Explicit means reproducible regardless of who runs it.
- **No `--reasoning-effort`, `--reasoning`, or `--quiet` flag exists** — set effort with `-c model_reasoning_effort="<level>"`; capture the last message with `-o file.txt`; capture stderr with `2>&1`.
- **`--sandbox workspace-write` blocks local IPC sockets, so a child cannot run checks that start `tsx`** — spec-kit's `npm --prefix runtime/cli run check` fails there with `listen EPERM`, also with `TMPDIR` pointed elsewhere (observed 2026-09-24 on codex-cli 0.156.1), and passes outside the sandbox. Tell the child which checks to leave to you, run them in the orchestrating session after it returns, and read that EPERM as a sandbox limit, not a code failure.

---

## 4. RULES

### ✅ ALWAYS

1. Verify Codex CLI is installed before first invocation (`command -v codex`).
2. Delegate research and review lineages to `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs` with executor kind `cli-codex`. It rejects every other loop type, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5. Never build a second adapter in this packet.
3. Use `--sandbox read-only` for review/analysis/research; `--sandbox workspace-write` for code generation/file modification — `codex exec` defaults to `read-only`, so omitting it causes silent no-op on edit tasks. For unattended approval, put top-level `-a never` before `exec` or set `-c approval_policy=never`.
4. Validate Codex-generated code (XSS, injection, eval, syntax checks via `node --check`, `tsc --noEmit`, etc.) before applying.
5. Capture stderr (`2>&1`) so rate-limit messages and errors surface.
6. **Redirect codex stdin from `/dev/null` on EVERY non-interactive dispatch** — not only inside a `while read` loop, which is the condition this rule used to name and the reason it was skipped. Pattern: `codex exec "$PROMPT" > "$LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null &`. Without `</dev/null`, the backgrounded codex process inherits the loop's stdin (the file after `done < input.jsonl`) and silently consumes the remaining lines — the loop exits after 3-6 iterations with no error. See `references/integration-patterns.md#background-execution` → "Silent Stdin Consumption".
7. **Specify model + effort + service tier explicitly** — never rely on caller environment. Default: `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="medium" -c service_tier="fast"`. Honor user overrides verbatim. Use `high`/`xhigh` for reasoning-heavy tasks (architecture, security, deep planning).
8. Route to the appropriate `-p <profile>` when the task matches a specialization (see Section 3 routing table); use `codex exec review` (built-in subcommand) for git diff reviews.
9. **Pass the spec folder to the delegated agent** in the prompt: if the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder, include `Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)`. If none, ASK the user before delegating — the delegated agent cannot answer Gate 3 in non-interactive mode.
10. **Prompt construction & model-craft (cli-* family precedence).** Compose every dispatch prompt via the 2-tier rule canonical in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md`:
   1. **Fast path (default).** Build from the local `assets/prompt-quality-card.md`, which delegates the framework table + CLEAR check to the canonical card.
   2. **Deep path (escalation).** Dispatch `@prompt-improver` via the Task tool (never load full `sk-prompt` inline) when any canonical **Tier 2** trigger applies — the trigger list lives in `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` under "Tier 2 — Deep path"; do not re-enumerate it here.

| "Use gpt 5.5 xhigh" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="xhigh" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| "Use gpt 6 luna max" | `--model gpt-6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort="max" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| "Use gpt 5.6 terra high" | `--model gpt-5.6-terra -c model_reasoning_effort="high" -c service_tier="fast"` |
| "Use gpt 6 sol ultra" | `--model gpt-6-sol -c model_reasoning_effort="ultra" -c service_tier="fast"` |

Honor whichever dimensions the user names. Model stays on `gpt-5.5` and service tier stays on `fast` unless the user explicitly names a different model or tier; keep the reasoning effort within the chosen model's ceiling (see Model Selection below and the roster in [references/providers-and-models.md](references/providers-and-models.md)).

### Model Selection

`gpt-5.5` at `medium` on the `fast` service tier (`-c service_tier="fast"`) is the skill default for cross-AI delegation. Alternates: `gpt-6-luna` (≤ `max`), `gpt-5.6-terra` / `gpt-6-sol` (≤ `ultra`) — full roster, per-model effort ceilings, and the 8-level effort ladder in [references/providers-and-models.md](references/providers-and-models.md). Set effort with `-c model_reasoning_effort="<level>"` (there is **no `--reasoning-effort` flag**).

**Selection Strategy**: default `gpt-5.5 medium`; raise to `high` / `xhigh` for architecture, security, and complex planning; escalate the model when the task wants reasoning past `xhigh`; drop to `low` / `minimal` for trivial lookups. Per-task rationale table: [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) §5.

### Codex Agent Delegation

The calling AI is the conductor; Codex profiles in `$CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml` shape HOW Codex processes the task (sandbox, reasoning). Route with `-p <name>` when the task matches a specialization. Full roster and invocation patterns: [agent-delegation.md](./references/agent-delegation.md).

| Task Type | Profile |
|-----------|---------|
| Code review / security audit | `review` |
| Architecture exploration | `context` |
| Technical research | `research` (+ top-level `--search`) |
| Documentation generation | `write` |
| Fresh-perspective debugging | `debug` |
| Multi-strategy planning | `ai-council` |

Git diff review uses the built-in subcommand (no `-p`): `codex exec review "..." --commit HEAD`. Profiles may override `model`, `model_reasoning_effort`, `sandbox_mode`, `approval_policy`. The `.codex/agents/*.toml` files define personas for the interactive multi-agent TUI, NOT the `-p` flag.

### Dispatch-Critical Gotchas

The full flag glossary, sandbox modes, unique capabilities (`/review`, `--search`, `codex mcp`, session resume/fork, `--image`, `codex cloud`), essential command examples, and troubleshooting table are in the ALWAYS-loaded [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md). Five gotchas that break a dispatch, or make a child misreport its result, and must be honored at routing time:

- **`codex exec` defaults to `--sandbox read-only`** — file-modification tasks silently no-op (the agent plans changes but cannot write them). Pass `--sandbox workspace-write`; for headless no-prompt execution use top-level `-a never` before `exec` or `-c approval_policy=never`.
- **`--search` is a top-level flag, not an `exec` flag** — enable live web search as `codex --search exec …` (it precedes the subcommand). On codex ≥ 0.144 `codex exec --search` hard-fails with `unexpected argument '--search'` (older 0.125 builds accepted it), so treat any `exec … --search` example as stale. Without it, `codex exec` has no web access and answers from training data only — every dispatch needing live data (latest versions, repo facts, advisories) MUST use `codex --search exec …`.
- **Always pass `-c service_tier="fast"` explicitly** — this routes through the fast tier instead of whatever the caller's `~/.codex/config.toml` defaults to. Explicit means reproducible regardless of who runs it.
- **No `--reasoning-effort`, `--reasoning`, or `--quiet` flag exists** — set effort with `-c model_reasoning_effort="<level>"`; capture the last message with `-o file.txt`; capture stderr with `2>&1`.
- **`--sandbox workspace-write` blocks local IPC sockets, so a child cannot run checks that start `tsx`** — spec-kit's `npm --prefix runtime/cli run check` fails there with `listen EPERM`, also with `TMPDIR` pointed elsewhere (observed 2026-09-24 on codex-cli 0.156.1), and passes outside the sandbox. Tell the child which checks to leave to you, run them in the orchestrating session after it returns, and read that EPERM as a sandbox limit, not a code failure.

---

## 4. RULES

### ✅ ALWAYS

1. Verify Codex CLI is installed before first invocation (`command -v codex`).
2. Delegate research and review lineages to `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs` with executor kind `cli-codex`. It rejects every other loop type, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5. Never build a second adapter in this packet.
3. Use `--sandbox read-only` for review/analysis/research; `--sandbox workspace-write` for code generation/file modification — `codex exec` defaults to `read-only`, so omitting it causes silent no-op on edit tasks. For unattended approval, put top-level `-a never` before `exec` or set `-c approval_policy=never`.
4. Validate Codex-generated code (XSS, injection, eval, syntax checks via `node --check`, `tsc --noEmit`, etc.) before applying.
5. Capture stderr (`2>&1`) so rate-limit messages and errors surface.
6. **Redirect codex stdin from `/dev/null` on EVERY non-interactive dispatch** — not only inside a `while read` loop, which is the condition this rule used to name and the reason it was skipped. 8. Route to the appropriate `-p <profile>` when the task matches a specialization (see Section 3 routing table); use `codex exec review` (built-in subcommand) for git diff reviews.
9. **Pass the spec folder to the delegated agent** in the prompt: if the calling AI has an active Gate-3 spec folder, include `Spec folder: <path> (pre-approved, skip Gate 3)`. If none, ASK the user before delegating — the delegated agent cannot answer Gate 3 in non-interactive mode.

_json_escape() {
  local s="$1"
  s="${s//\\/\\\\}"
  s="${s//\"/\\\"}"

  s="${s//$'\r'/\\r}"

}

# Show_help()

  local loc=$1

## PHASE DOCUMENTATION MAP

> This spec uses phased decomposition. Each phase is an independently executable child spec folder. All implementation details (plan, tasks, checklist, decisions, continuity) live inside the phase children.

| Phase | Folder | Focus | Status |
|-------|--------|-------|--------|
| 1 | 001-template-drift-census-and-baseline/ | Census every template, example and reference defect into a verified ledger and measure the authoring baseline | Pending |
| 2 | 002-template-and-example-defect-repair/ | Apply the ledger rows owned by this phase with a tested exact-match applier | Pending |
| 3 | 003-versioned-placeholder-gate/ | Make unfilled `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ...]` tokens a Draft warning and a later error, for v2.3 docs only | Pending |
| 4 | 004-template-section-fill-guidance/ | Add a fill instruction and a good and weak example to each core section, and guard example drift | Pending |
| 5 | 005-weak-model-authoring-card/ | Write the authoring card, route the skill to it and guard the sync | Pending |
| 6 | 006-speckit-command-and-agent-alignment/ | Check and update the speckit and doctor commands and the doc-authoring agents such as markdown for the new templates, gate and card | Pending |
| 7 | 007-playbook-catalog-readme-alignment/ | Update the playbook, catalog and READMEs for the new behavior | Pending |
| 8 | 008-playbook-run-in-worktree/ | Run every new or changed playbook scenario in a disposable worktree and report PASS or FAIL | Pending |
| 9 | 009-authoring-benchmark-and-closeout/ | Rerun the baseline, report the delta per metric and close the packet | Pending |

### Phase Transition Rules

- Each phase MUST pass `validate.sh` independently before the next phase begins
- Parent spec tracks aggregate progress via this map
- Use `/spec_kit:resume [parent-folder]/[NNN-phase]/` to resume a specific phase
- Run `validate.sh --recursive` on parent to validate all phases as integrated unit

### Phase Handoff Criteria

| From | To | Criteria | Verification |
|------|-----|----------|--------------|
| 001-template-drift-census-and-baseline | 002-template-and-example-defect-repair | `ledger.jsonl` exists, every row reproduces and the baseline holds three runs | `jq -c . ledger.jsonl` exits 0 and `baseline.json` holds 3 runs |
| 002-template-and-example-defect-repair | 003-versioned-placeholder-gate | Every owner-002 row no longer reproduces and the suite result matches the phase 001 start | Row evidence commands print nothing and the suite summary lines match `suite-start.txt` |
| 003-versioned-placeholder-gate | 004-template-section-fill-guidance | Core hints are tokens, the marker is v2.3 and recursive strict counts are unchanged | The failing-first test passes and the before and after counts match |
| 004-template-section-fill-guidance | 005-weak-model-authoring-card | Every core section has guidance, goldens pass and the drift guard passes | The golden test and the drift guard script exit 0 |
| 005-weak-model-authoring-card | 006-speckit-command-and-agent-alignment | The card exists, the router loads it and the sync guard passes | The sync guard script exits 0 and the workflow invariance test passes |
| 006-speckit-command-and-agent-alignment | 007-playbook-catalog-readme-alignment | Every speckit and doctor command and every doc-authoring agent names the card, the v2.3 token and the guard scripts where it describes authoring | The phase 006 audit table has no open row |
| 007-playbook-catalog-readme-alignment | 008-playbook-run-in-worktree | Every new scenario file exists and the playbook index lists it | The playbook index lists each scenario id |
| 008-playbook-run-in-worktree | 009-authoring-benchmark-and-closeout | Every scenario has a recorded PASS or an escalated FAIL | The report folder holds a row for each scenario |
<!-- /ANCHOR:phase-map -->

USAGE:
  recommend-level.sh [OPTIONS]

  --loc <number>       Lines of code estimate (required)

# Uses linear interpolation between thresholds
calculate_loc_score() {
  local loc=$1
  local score=0

  if [[ "$loc" -le "$LOC_THRESHOLD_LOW" ]]; then
    # 0-50 LOC: 0-8 points (linear)
    score=$((loc * 8 / LOC_THRESHOLD_LOW))
  elif [[ "$loc" -le "$LOC_THRESHOLD_MED" ]]; then
    # 51-150 LOC: 8-18 points
    local range=$((LOC_THRESHOLD_MED - LOC_THRESHOLD_LOW))
    local offset=$((loc - LOC_THRESHOLD_LOW))
    score=$((8 + (offset * 10 / range)))

    # 151-400 LOC: 18-28 points
